v1.feedback: The concentric-ring + spoke attractor scaffold is a smart way to channel physarum into a medallion silhouette, and the gold palette genuinely evokes talisman warmth — but the 12-fold radial symmetry risks reading as a generic mandala rather than a physarum form that was *transformed* by the word. Let the spoke count be odd (7 or 9) and break perfect rotational symmetry so the organic weave texture of the parent shows through the geometric scaffold. The attractor pull strength needs careful tuning: too strong and agents just trace circles (losing physarum character), too weak and it dissolves into a centered blob — expose that balance as a time-varying parameter so the form breathes between order and growth. Consider a faint inner glow or brighter deposit weight on the innermost ring to give the talisman a visible 'core' that anchors the eye in under 2 seconds.

v2.feedback: The talisman concept genuinely drove the scaffold — 9-fold asymmetric spokes, concentric rings, breathing pull dynamics, warm gold palette — and the parent's physarum agent sim is preserved, not discarded. But 'continuous morph of parent' is under-delivered: this reads as a fresh physarum run with talisman-shaped attractors, not as 3qt's form being transformed by the word. The display shader only reads trail.r while the deposit fragment writes to both r and g channels for the two populations — population B's green deposit is wasted visually, collapsing the dual-population structure to monoculture on screen. CPU readback of a 1024×1024 float texture every frame will stutter on most hardware; consider a GPU-only trail-sense pass or downsample the readback to 512² to keep the breathing animation smooth.
